title: Web client
summary: The Three.js client: staging, director, camera, UI and headless tools.
bodyHtml:
web/ renders the game in real time with Three.js. It adds no rules: every decision goes through Game.choose, and the client turns the difference between the state before and after into something you watch. Nothing is downloaded but Three.js: every model, texture and sound is built in code.

Staging

  • World (web/src/world/): a procedural road through six regions, terrain displaced in a shader using the same noise as the props, wagon train, figures, gear, birds, sky and haze.
  • The sky is the gauge: stars and teal cloud far away; stains spread, the moon reddens, fog turns crimson, blood pools in ruts, ash falls, and the Haze rises as a churning wall at the sim's gap distance.
  • Fire is the light: torch poles on wagons, the wagon-master walking ahead with a torch, a camp ring when torches burned.
  • Travel is a side-on and portrait 3/4 tracking shot of the caravan to show its diminishing state.

Director

web/src/director.ts plays each transition: making and breaking camp, rolling to the next event, strangers staged on the road, recruits walking over, the dead falling with a grave marker left, crises in camp, combat, and the four endings. Stage pieces live in web/src/scenes/ (vignettes.ts, combat.ts, fork.ts, pieces.ts). Talk staging: web/src/talk/.

Camera

web/src/world/camera.ts: shots are functions the director hands over; the camera frames the subject in the part of the screen the card leaves free. Cinematics letterbox and can be skipped with a click or Space. Dialogue cuts to an angle that shows a hidden speaker.

UI

web/src/ui/: a thin HTML layer with a HUD gauge showing the red band chasing your wagon, a party dock, each decision as a card, speech bubbles, tell cues, diegetic rolls, and a parchment map. Sound is procedural WebAudio (web/src/audio.ts). Quality scales down on phones.

Headless tools

  • tools/web-scene.mjs: render one situation to a PNG, using scene scripts in tools/scenes/.
  • tools/web-play.mjs: play through the real UI in headless Chromium, screenshot each new screen kind, sample geometry and texture counts in PROBE mode.
  • tools/web-talk-click.mjs: click through dialogue.
  • tools/video/overlay-shot.mjs: screenshot the video overlay.

The client is a prototype presentation layer, not a second engine. The director's job (turn a before/after diff into staging) is the part to carry into Dream Engine. See Build, test and verify.
